(NASDAQ:MAT) from its intrinsic value? Using the most recent financial data, we'll take a look at whether the stock is fairly priced by taking the expected future cash flows and discounting them to their present value. This will be done using the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model. It may sound complicated, but actually it is quite simple!Companies can be valued in a lot of ways, so we would point out that a DCF is not perfect for every situation. Anyone interested in learning a bit more about intrinsic value should have a read of the Simply Wall St analysis model. Check out our latest analysis for Mattel The MethodWe are going to use a two-stage DCF model, which, as the name states, takes into account two stages of growth. The first stage is generally a higher growth period which levels off heading towards the terminal value, captured in the second 'steady growth' period. To start off with, we need to estimate the next ten years of cash flows. Where possible we use analyst estimates, but when these aren't available we extrapolate the previous free cash flow (FCF) from the last estimate or reported value. We assume companies with shrinking free cash flow will slow their rate of shrinkage, and that companies with growing free cash flow will see their growth rate slow, over this period. We do this to reflect that growth tends to slow more in the early years than it does in later years.Generally we assume that a dollar today is more valuable than a dollar in the future, and so the sum of these future cash flows is then discounted to today's value:10-year free cash flow (FCF) forecast2024202520262027202820292030203120322033 Levered FCF ($, Millions) US$564.3mUS$734.0mUS$687.0mUS$735.0mUS$771.7mUS$803.7mUS$832.2mUS$858.2mUS$882.5mUS$905.7mGrowth Rate Estimate SourceAnalyst x4Analyst x1Analyst x1Analyst x1Est @ 5.00%Est @ 4.14%Est @ 3.54%Est @ 3.13%Est @ 2.83%Est @ 2.63% Present Value ($, Millions) Discounted @ 8.8% US$519US$620US$534US$525US$507US$485US$462US$438US$414US$391("Est" = FCF growth rate estimated by Simply Wall St)Present Value of 10-year Cash Flow (PVCF) = US$4.9bStory continuesThe second stage is also known as Terminal Value, this is the business's cash flow after the first stage. For a number of reasons a very conservative growth rate is used that cannot exceed that of a country's GDP growth. In this case we have used the 5-year average of the 10-year government bond yield (2.2%) to estimate future growth. In the same way as with the 10-year 'growth' period, we discount future cash flows to today's value, using a cost of equity of 8.8%.Terminal Value (TV)= FCF2033 × (1 + g) ÷ (r – g) = US$906m× (1 + 2.2%) ÷ (8.8%– 2.2%) = US$14bPresent Value of Terminal Value (PVTV)= TV / (1 + r)10= US$14b÷ ( 1 + 8.8%)10= US$6.0bThe total value, or equity value, is then the sum of the present value of the future cash flows, which in this case is US$11b. The last step is to then divide the equity value by the number of shares outstanding. Compared to the current share price of US$21.3, the company appears quite good value at a 31% discount to where the stock price trades currently. The assumptions in any calculation have a big impact on the valuation, so it is better to view this as a rough estimate, not precise down to the last cent.dcfThe AssumptionsWe would point out that the most important inputs to a discounted cash flow are the discount rate and of course the actual cash flows. Part of investing is coming up with your own evaluation of a company's future performance, so try the calculation yourself and check your own assumptions. The DCF also does not consider the possible cyclicality of an industry, or a company's future capital requirements, so it does not give a full picture of a company's potential performance. Given that we are looking at Mattel as potential shareholders, the cost of equity is used as the discount rate, rather than the cost of capital (or weighted average cost of capital, WACC) which accounts for debt. In this calculation we've used 8.8%, which is based on a levered beta of 1.324. Beta is a measure of a stock's volatility, compared to the market as a whole. We get our beta from the industry average beta of globally comparable companies, with an imposed limit between 0.8 and 2.0, which is a reasonable range for a stable business.SWOT Analysis for MattelStrengthDebt is well covered by earnings and cashflows.WeaknessEarnings declined over the past year.OpportunityAnnual earnings are forecast to grow faster than the American market.Trading below our estimate of fair value by more than 20%.ThreatAnnual revenue is forecast to grow slower than the American market.Moving On:Although the valuation of a company is important, it is only one of many factors that you need to assess for a company. Title: 'Barbie' movie: Mattel's gross billings to rise by $125M thanks to film, CEO says
Text: [Barbie has dominated the summer box office grossing over $1.4B worldwide. One of the big beneficiaries has been the company that makes the toy, Mattel (MAT). Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz sat down with Yahoo Finance’s Brian Sozzi to discuss all things Barbie, Mattel, and how the company has shifted in it's approach. According to Kreiz, gross billings, as a direct result of the Barbie movie, will increase by $125 million, at about a 60% operating income margin.Bigger picture, Kreiz explains the company's approach in “long-term franchise management” and how the company evolved from a toy manufacturing company to “an IP company that manages franchises”, using “cultural events to benefit the company for years to come." "It's more than a toy. What we create is more than a play system. It's a holistic approach to engage with your fans across multiple levels," Kreiz zays, adding that the opportunities are beyond just films.Click here for more of Yahoo Finance's coverage from the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference.Video TranscriptBRIAN SOZZI: Mattel chairman and CEO Ynon Kreiz. Ynon, where's-- Will Ferrell's behind you somewhere, right? I'm looking for him, no?YNON KREIZ: Great to see you, Brian. Thank you for having me.BRIAN SOZZI: So what is next on the Barbie front? We're starting to see every week the gross theater receipts continue to increase. You're approaching $2 billion. What is next for this franchise?YNON KREIZ: Well, we couldn't be more excited about the way the movie played out to resounding success, a real execution of Greta Gerwig's vision. And what we're seeing coming out of it, three things. It's the strength and cultural resonance of our brands, is our ability to attract, collaborate, and partner with top creative talent, and our ability to promote and create a cultural event of this movie, leveraging our commercial capabilities in partnership with Warner Brothers, who did a terrific job marketing the movie. So it's been a real combination driven by strong brand and great execution, both creatively and commercially.Story continuesBRIAN SOZZI: Your CFO gave a presentation earlier this morning, I think, for the first time, shared some numbers on how much Mattel may make from this movie. Can you share some of those numbers? And what does it mean for the future financial performance of the company?YNON KREIZ: Yes, we did talk about our revenue, gross billing this year to go up by about $125 million from movie, direct movie participation, toys, and consumer products directly related to the movie, not other Barbie product, at a 60%-- sorry, yeah, 60% operating income margin. So about $75 million operating income contribution directly related to the movie in 2023.BRIAN SOZZI: Is that higher than your expectations? Because from an outside looking in, that's a huge number. And in many respects, Ynon, that's a number that you didn't have last year on the financial statements.YNON KREIZ: Well, we did not expect the movie to be as successful. So it is more than we assumed entering the year. And we expect that in future years, there will be continued benefit from the movie. This is about long-term franchise management. It's not just about the quarter or the year.And we-- it's the thing that we've always talked about, you and me. This was the approach. It was never about just trying to sell more toys. It was about creating a cultural event, creating a societal moment. And we believe the benefit will carry forward for years to come.BRIAN SOZZI: We've talked a lot throughout the years. And this is the first time I've heard you mention franchise management. What does that mean as it pertains to now this cultural juggernaut that you've created? Of course, the Barbie brand has been there for decades. But now you have the movie, you have the content component. How do you manage this?YNON KREIZ: We started our journey as a toy company, as a toy manufacturing company. We evolved to be an IP company that manages franchises. And the biggest change in how we approach our business is to realize that people who buy our products and not just consumers, they are fans. And once you have a lot of fans, it's an audience.And when you realize that you have an audience, it changes the conversation. And the opportunity for you to continue to grow your business. And given that we own one of the strongest portfolios in children and family entertainment franchises in the world, this creates a very unique and exciting opportunities-- opportunity for us to grow outside of the toy aisle into highly accretive business verticals driven by big brands and big franchises, which we own. And the "Barbie" movie, we look-- we see as a template, as an example, in terms of how we approach franchise management and expect more to come.BRIAN SOZZI: You have a portfolio of really amazing toy brands that all of us in many respects have grown up using. How do you take this playbook and apply it to some of these brands? What will we see from Mattel over the next 24 months?YNON KREIZ: Our brands are very much timely as much as they are timeless. And we've been doing a lot of work around infusing cultural relevance and societal awareness for what we do with a very strong purpose behind our brands. So it's more than a toy. What we create is more than a play system. It's a holistic approach to engaging-- engage with your fans across multiple levels.And the opportunity for us is not just film. It's also television. It's video games. It's location-based entertainment. It's musicals. It's-- whatever medium is driven by big franchises and big brands. In today's world, this is what it's all about-- big brands, big franchises that elevate and rise above a crowded marketplace. And we believe we are at the beginning of a very exciting part of our journey.BRIAN SOZZI: Well, it's going to be hard to create another nearly $2 billion movie. It just doesn't happen very often. But within the portfolios that you and the portfolio brands you own, what's the brand you're really focused on that you're going to run this playbook with next?YNON KREIZ: Yeah. We're not saying every movie that we make will be as successful, but it will be the same approach, the same methodology, and the same creative take that we are looking to apply. There's the "Hot Wheels" movie that we're developing with JJ Abrams. There's a Matchbox movie with Skydance, which produced "Mission Impossible" and "Top Gun." There's a movie we're developing with Vin Diesel for Rock'em Sock'em Robots, Polly Pocket with Lena Dunham and Lily Collins, and Major Matt Mason with Tom Hanks written by Akiva Goldsman.So these are just a few examples of some of the projects that we're developing. And you can see, given the quality and strength and proven track record of our partners, we believe we have a real shot at creating exciting projects that will appeal to global audiences. And what we saw within the "Barbie" movie is that the picture appealed not just to the core buyers of Barbie toys, Barbie product, this was a much broader approach to global audiences across different demographics, men and women, different ages, different generations. And everyone found something that talked to them and touch them at an emotional level.And the credit goes to the incredible execution of this project by Greta Gerwig, who had such a vision and, of course, Margot Robbie as a producer and a lead actor, Ryan Gosling, and, of course, the soundtrack that was a key part of the holistic experience, all of it created something very special that we're very proud of.BRIAN SOZZI: This-- this didn't happen overnight. But my sense has been that you saw the potential of this happening many years ago when you took over at Mattel. From a leadership perspective, how did you identify that? And then how do you ultimately go about bringing that to life?YNON KREIZ: Yeah. This journey has been long in the making, started about five years ago. And from the very beginning, the approach was to create something that was not conventional, something that was not traditional. And the term "cultural event" is what we said back in the day. It was never about trying to make a movie or, for that matter, make a movie in order to sell toys.The focus was to create a quality content, quality content that people will want to watch. And we know that if we do that, and if we do that well, good things will happen. And we will sell a lot of toys. So it's not that we didn't want to sell toys, but the mandate and the approach and the relationship and the engagement with the creatives that partnered with us was to focus on making a great movie and not think about selling toys.And what we see now, of course, we have a great movie. We see the success at the box office. And we also are starting to see the success on the toy side of the company with POS for the company year-to-date up, Barbie gaining momentum. And overall, we see good, very exciting opportunity for us to continue to gain share.BRIAN SOZZI: Seemingly, every day, over the past three months, I've read another story about the "Barbie" movie, something new happening. But also, you, you've been front and center in a lot of these stories and on, as you should be, because you brought this to life, this cultural event. How have you stayed grounded? And how do you look-- how are you looking to stay grounded over the next few months when you have all these publications writing about you, telling you how successful you are? And how do you just stay focused with all this frenzy around yourself?YNON KREIZ: Well, this very much has been a team effort. It's been a journey with a lot of people that participated and made it all happen. And I couldn't be more proud of the team and everything that we've done collectively. For this to be successful, for this movie to be where it is today, it took a lot of effort. And I'm grateful for everyone's support and involvement.And we really do see it as a beginning of a new chapter. This is not a one-off movie. It's not a one-off project. This has been the strategy. And you followed our story, and you know that we've been consistently made progress in building and driving our IP strategy to reach this point.But it's not the moment we've been waiting to arrive, and we're done by any stretch. This is really one-- another step in the journey. We see it as a template. We see it as an example. As I said before, this is the approach. And we look to replicate that approach in terms of leveraging our brands that have been foundational in this case specifically-- you know, Barbie, it's the "Barbie" movie-- working with top talent that have a clear vision and are the best in what they do, which we have done in this movie as well. And of course, commercializing and executing the marketing level and creating demand in a marketplace that became a cultural phenomenon. And so this has been a great and exciting journey. And we're still very much at the early stage of it.BRIAN SOZZI: Thanks for making a little time for little old me and on. I appreciate it. I know you're the big star now. But I appreciate it. Thanks for always giving time to Yahoo Finance. It's been fun to follow this journey. I mean, hat tip to you and your team. Ynon Kreiz, Chairman and CEO of Mattel.Seana, back to you in New York. I know you're a big fan of the "Barbie" movie.SEANA SMITH: I am a big fan of the "Barbie" movie. We've been talking about it for over a year. So, of course, our thanks to you, saw all the great interviews out there, and Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz as well.]

The first stage is generally a higher growth period which levels off heading towards the terminal value, captured in the second 'steady growth' period. To start off with, we need to estimate the next ten years of cash flows. Where possible we use analyst estimates, but when these aren't available we extrapolate the previous free cash flow (FCF) from the last estimate or reported value. We assume companies with shrinking free cash flow will slow their rate of shrinkage, and that companies with growing free cash flow will see their growth rate slow, over this period. We do this to reflect that growth tends to slow more in the early years than it does in later years.Generally we assume that a dollar today is more valuable than a dollar in the future, and so the sum of these future cash flows is then discounted to today's value:10-year free cash flow (FCF) forecast2024202520262027202820292030203120322033 Levered FCF ($, Millions) US$564.3mUS$734.0mUS$687.0mUS$735.0mUS$771.7mUS$803.7mUS$832.2mUS$858.2mUS$882.5mUS$905.7mGrowth Rate Estimate SourceAnalyst x4Analyst x1Analyst x1Analyst x1Est @ 5.00%Est @ 4.14%Est @ 3.54%Est @ 3.13%Est @ 2.83%Est @ 2.63% Present Value ($, Millions) Discounted @ 8.8% US$519US$620US$534US$525US$507US$485US$462US$438US$414US$391("Est" = FCF growth rate estimated by Simply Wall St)Present Value of 10-year Cash Flow (PVCF) = US$4.9bStory continuesThe second stage is also known as Terminal Value, this is the business's cash flow after the first stage. For a number of reasons a very conservative growth rate is used that cannot exceed that of a country's GDP growth. In this case we have used the 5-year average of the 10-year government bond yield (2.2%) to estimate future growth. In the same way as with the 10-year 'growth' period, we discount future cash flows to today's value, using a cost of equity of 8.8%.Terminal Value (TV)= FCF2033 × (1 + g) ÷ (r – g) = US$906m× (1 + 2.2%) ÷ (8.8%– 2.2%) = US$14bPresent Value of Terminal Value (PVTV)= TV / (1 + r)10= US$14b÷ ( 1 + 8.8%)10= US$6.0bThe total value, or equity value, is then the sum of the present value of the future cash flows, which in this case is US$11b. The last step is to then divide the equity value by the number of shares outstanding. Compared to the current share price of US$21.3, the company appears quite good value at a 31% discount to where the stock price trades currently. The assumptions in any calculation have a big impact on the valuation, so it is better to view this as a rough estimate, not precise down to the last cent.dcfThe AssumptionsWe would point out that the most important inputs to a discounted cash flow are the discount rate and of course the actual cash flows. Part of investing is coming up with your own evaluation of a company's future performance, so try the calculation yourself and check your own assumptions. The DCF also does not consider the possible cyclicality of an industry, or a company's future capital requirements, so it does not give a full picture of a company's potential performance. Given that we are looking at Mattel as potential shareholders, the cost of equity is used as the discount rate, rather than the cost of capital (or weighted average cost of capital, WACC) which accounts for debt. In this calculation we've used 8.8%, which is based on a levered beta of 1.324. Beta is a measure of a stock's volatility, compared to the market as a whole. We get our beta from the industry average beta of globally comparable companies, with an imposed limit between 0.8 and 2.0, which is a reasonable range for a stable business.SWOT Analysis for MattelStrengthDebt is well covered by earnings and cashflows.WeaknessEarnings declined over the past year.OpportunityAnnual earnings are forecast to grow faster than the American market.Trading below our estimate of fair value by more than 20%.ThreatAnnual revenue is forecast to grow slower than the American market.Moving On:Although the valuation of a company is important, it is only one of many factors that you need to assess for a company. The DCF model is not a perfect stock valuation tool. Preferably you'd apply different cases and assumptions and see how they would impact the company's valuation. Title: 'Barbie' movie: Mattel's gross billings to rise by $125M thanks to film, CEO says
Text: [Barbie has dominated the summer box office grossing over $1.4B worldwide. One of the big beneficiaries has been the company that makes the toy, Mattel (MAT). Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz sat down with Yahoo Finance’s Brian Sozzi to discuss all things Barbie, Mattel, and how the company has shifted in it's approach. According to Kreiz, gross billings, as a direct result of the Barbie movie, will increase by $125 million, at about a 60% operating income margin.Bigger picture, Kreiz explains the company's approach in “long-term franchise management” and how the company evolved from a toy manufacturing company to “an IP company that manages franchises”, using “cultural events to benefit the company for years to come." "It's more than a toy. What we create is more than a play system. It's a holistic approach to engage with your fans across multiple levels," Kreiz zays, adding that the opportunities are beyond just films.Click here for more of Yahoo Finance's coverage from the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference.Video TranscriptBRIAN SOZZI: Mattel chairman and CEO Ynon Kreiz. Ynon, where's-- Will Ferrell's behind you somewhere, right? I'm looking for him, no?YNON KREIZ: Great to see you, Brian. Thank you for having me.BRIAN SOZZI: So what is next on the Barbie front? We're starting to see every week the gross theater receipts continue to increase. You're approaching $2 billion. What is next for this franchise?YNON KREIZ: Well, we couldn't be more excited about the way the movie played out to resounding success, a real execution of Greta Gerwig's vision. And what we're seeing coming out of it, three things. It's the strength and cultural resonance of our brands, is our ability to attract, collaborate, and partner with top creative talent, and our ability to promote and create a cultural event of this movie, leveraging our commercial capabilities in partnership with Warner Brothers, who did a terrific job marketing the movie. So it's been a real combination driven by strong brand and great execution, both creatively and commercially.Story continuesBRIAN SOZZI: Your CFO gave a presentation earlier this morning, I think, for the first time, shared some numbers on how much Mattel may make from this movie. Can you share some of those numbers? And what does it mean for the future financial performance of the company?YNON KREIZ: Yes, we did talk about our revenue, gross billing this year to go up by about $125 million from movie, direct movie participation, toys, and consumer products directly related to the movie, not other Barbie product, at a 60%-- sorry, yeah, 60% operating income margin. So about $75 million operating income contribution directly related to the movie in 2023.BRIAN SOZZI: Is that higher than your expectations? Because from an outside looking in, that's a huge number. And in many respects, Ynon, that's a number that you didn't have last year on the financial statements.YNON KREIZ: Well, we did not expect the movie to be as successful. So it is more than we assumed entering the year. And we expect that in future years, there will be continued benefit from the movie. This is about long-term franchise management. It's not just about the quarter or the year.And we-- it's the thing that we've always talked about, you and me. This was the approach. It was never about just trying to sell more toys. It was about creating a cultural event, creating a societal moment. And we believe the benefit will carry forward for years to come.BRIAN SOZZI: We've talked a lot throughout the years. And this is the first time I've heard you mention franchise management. What does that mean as it pertains to now this cultural juggernaut that you've created? Of course, the Barbie brand has been there for decades. But now you have the movie, you have the content component. How do you manage this?YNON KREIZ: We started our journey as a toy company, as a toy manufacturing company. We evolved to be an IP company that manages franchises. And the biggest change in how we approach our business is to realize that people who buy our products and not just consumers, they are fans. And once you have a lot of fans, it's an audience.And when you realize that you have an audience, it changes the conversation. And the opportunity for you to continue to grow your business. And given that we own one of the strongest portfolios in children and family entertainment franchises in the world, this creates a very unique and exciting opportunities-- opportunity for us to grow outside of the toy aisle into highly accretive business verticals driven by big brands and big franchises, which we own. And the "Barbie" movie, we look-- we see as a template, as an example, in terms of how we approach franchise management and expect more to come.BRIAN SOZZI: You have a portfolio of really amazing toy brands that all of us in many respects have grown up using. How do you take this playbook and apply it to some of these brands? What will we see from Mattel over the next 24 months?YNON KREIZ: Our brands are very much timely as much as they are timeless. And we've been doing a lot of work around infusing cultural relevance and societal awareness for what we do with a very strong purpose behind our brands. So it's more than a toy. What we create is more than a play system. It's a holistic approach to engaging-- engage with your fans across multiple levels.And the opportunity for us is not just film. It's also television. It's video games. It's location-based entertainment. It's musicals. It's-- whatever medium is driven by big franchises and big brands. In today's world, this is what it's all about-- big brands, big franchises that elevate and rise above a crowded marketplace. And we believe we are at the beginning of a very exciting part of our journey.BRIAN SOZZI: Well, it's going to be hard to create another nearly $2 billion movie. It just doesn't happen very often. But within the portfolios that you and the portfolio brands you own, what's the brand you're really focused on that you're going to run this playbook with next?YNON KREIZ: Yeah. We're not saying every movie that we make will be as successful, but it will be the same approach, the same methodology, and the same creative take that we are looking to apply. There's the "Hot Wheels" movie that we're developing with JJ Abrams. There's a Matchbox movie with Skydance, which produced "Mission Impossible" and "Top Gun." There's a movie we're developing with Vin Diesel for Rock'em Sock'em Robots, Polly Pocket with Lena Dunham and Lily Collins, and Major Matt Mason with Tom Hanks written by Akiva Goldsman.So these are just a few examples of some of the projects that we're developing. And you can see, given the quality and strength and proven track record of our partners, we believe we have a real shot at creating exciting projects that will appeal to global audiences. And what we saw within the "Barbie" movie is that the picture appealed not just to the core buyers of Barbie toys, Barbie product, this was a much broader approach to global audiences across different demographics, men and women, different ages, different generations. And everyone found something that talked to them and touch them at an emotional level.And the credit goes to the incredible execution of this project by Greta Gerwig, who had such a vision and, of course, Margot Robbie as a producer and a lead actor, Ryan Gosling, and, of course, the soundtrack that was a key part of the holistic experience, all of it created something very special that we're very proud of.BRIAN SOZZI: This-- this didn't happen overnight. But my sense has been that you saw the potential of this happening many years ago when you took over at Mattel. From a leadership perspective, how did you identify that? And then how do you ultimately go about bringing that to life?YNON KREIZ: Yeah. This journey has been long in the making, started about five years ago. And from the very beginning, the approach was to create something that was not conventional, something that was not traditional. And the term "cultural event" is what we said back in the day. It was never about trying to make a movie or, for that matter, make a movie in order to sell toys.The focus was to create a quality content, quality content that people will want to watch. And we know that if we do that, and if we do that well, good things will happen. And we will sell a lot of toys. So it's not that we didn't want to sell toys, but the mandate and the approach and the relationship and the engagement with the creatives that partnered with us was to focus on making a great movie and not think about selling toys.And what we see now, of course, we have a great movie. We see the success at the box office. And we also are starting to see the success on the toy side of the company with POS for the company year-to-date up, Barbie gaining momentum. And overall, we see good, very exciting opportunity for us to continue to gain share.BRIAN SOZZI: Seemingly, every day, over the past three months, I've read another story about the "Barbie" movie, something new happening. But also, you, you've been front and center in a lot of these stories and on, as you should be, because you brought this to life, this cultural event. How have you stayed grounded? And how do you look-- how are you looking to stay grounded over the next few months when you have all these publications writing about you, telling you how successful you are? And how do you just stay focused with all this frenzy around yourself?YNON KREIZ: Well, this very much has been a team effort. It's been a journey with a lot of people that participated and made it all happen. And I couldn't be more proud of the team and everything that we've done collectively. For this to be successful, for this movie to be where it is today, it took a lot of effort. And I'm grateful for everyone's support and involvement.And we really do see it as a beginning of a new chapter. This is not a one-off movie. It's not a one-off project. This has been the strategy. And you followed our story, and you know that we've been consistently made progress in building and driving our IP strategy to reach this point.But it's not the moment we've been waiting to arrive, and we're done by any stretch. This is really one-- another step in the journey. We see it as a template. We see it as an example. As I said before, this is the approach. And we look to replicate that approach in terms of leveraging our brands that have been foundational in this case specifically-- you know, Barbie, it's the "Barbie" movie-- working with top talent that have a clear vision and are the best in what they do, which we have done in this movie as well. And of course, commercializing and executing the marketing level and creating demand in a marketplace that became a cultural phenomenon. And so this has been a great and exciting journey. And we're still very much at the early stage of it.BRIAN SOZZI: Thanks for making a little time for little old me and on. I appreciate it. I know you're the big star now. But I appreciate it. Thanks for always giving time to Yahoo Finance. It's been fun to follow this journey. I mean, hat tip to you and your team. Ynon Kreiz, Chairman and CEO of Mattel.Seana, back to you in New York. I know you're a big fan of the "Barbie" movie.SEANA SMITH: I am a big fan of the "Barbie" movie. We've been talking about it for over a year. So, of course, our thanks to you, saw all the great interviews out there, and Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz as well.]

Title: Mattel (MAT) Gains 32% in 6 Months: Will the Rally Continue?
Text: [Mattel, Inc.’s MAT growth is attributable to its solid product portfolio, execution of the Optimizing for Growth program and focus on IP-driven offerings.Shares of MAT have gained 31.5% in the past six months, outperforming the Zacks Toys - Games - Hobbies industry’s 17.4% growth.This toy manufacturer delivered a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 84.2%, on average. Earnings estimates for 2023 have moved north from $1.16 per share to $1.19 per share, over the past 60 days. The company is benefiting from increased demand for Hot Wheels, the launch of new products aligned with the Barbie movie and the execution of its IP-driven toy business strategy.Zacks Investment ResearchImage Source: Zacks Investment ResearchHowever, this Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) company is facing headwinds in the form of macroeconomic uncertainties and an ongoing inflationary environment.Factors That Make the Stock AppealingDiverse Product Portfolio: Mattel benefits from a robust assortment of products encompassing core brands, licensed brands and profitable product affiliations. Brands like Hot Wheels, which accumulate a notable share of popularity, have been the category leader in multiple product segments of the company for several years. During the second quarter of 2023, gross billings at the Hot Wheels brand rose 10% (on a reported basis) and 9% (at constant currency) to $315.2 million, year over year. The company has been witnessing an improving sales trend for Hot Wheels and is quite confident about the brand’s long-term prospects. Moreover, its initiatives of product portfolio expansion, along with other digital expansions, add to the growth trend.Apart from Hot Wheels, MAT’s multi-year global licensing agreement with Disney has enabled it to lay down a variety of products, including Princess and Frozen branded line of products. This has driven the company’s second-quarter results and is consistently building momentum along with Monster High. Also, the company’s launch of a variety of toys and products related to the Barbie movie has created demand in the market, being sold out across major distribution channels from release to date. Furthermore, on Jul 25, 2023, the company renewed its multi-category licensing partnership with Warner Bros. Discovery Global Consumer Products. The product lines will include the DC Universe, Bat Wheels and Harry Potter, Fantastic Beasts, FRIENDS, among others.Optimizing for Growth Program: MAT’s initiation of a new multi-year program, Optimizing for Growth, in 2021 has contributed about $106 million of incremental savings in the cost of goods in 2022. In the second quarter of 2023, the company generated $24 million in savings through the execution of the Optimizing for Growth program. The company is on track for the program to deliver its savings goal of $300 million by 2023. Through the cost-saving program, it remains focused on achieving cumulative cost savings, thus, enhancing margins.IP-Driven Business Strategy: Mattel continues to make progress toward capturing the full value of its IP and transforming itself into a high-performing toy company. Title: MATTEL, NICKELODEON AND PARAMOUNT+ DEBUT TRAILER FOR MONSTER HIGH 2, THE SEQUEL TO THE LIVE-ACTION MUSICAL PREMIERING THURSDAY, OCT. 5
Text: [Movie will Introduce New Character Toralei, Feisty British Were-CatShare it: @Nickelodeon @Mattel @ParamountPlus @MonsterHigh #Nickelodeon #MonsterHigh2Click HERE to embed the trailer and HERE to download assets.EL SEGUNDO, Calif. and HOLLYWOOD, Calif., Sept. 15, 2023 /PRNewswire/ -- Mattel, Inc. (NASDAQ: MAT), Nickelodeon and Paramount+ today revealed the trailer and premiere date for Monster High 2, the sequel to the live-action movie musical based on the iconic Monster High franchise about the children of famous monsters and creatures. The power of three is put to the test as they face even bigger challenges this year—new students, new powers, evolving friendships, and an even bigger threat that could not only tear their friendship apart, but could change the world forever. The movie will also introduce new character Toralei (Salena Qureshi), a feisty British were-cat, back after a year abroad in Scaris, France.Monster High 2 also stars: Case Walker (The Other Two) as Deuce Gorgon; Marci T. The franchise seeks to foster a more accepting world where everyone is proud to be their authentic self, which is more relevant than ever. Today, Monster High is back with a reimagined set of fangtastic characters reflected in a new set of dolls, accessories, apparel, costumes and more, inspired by the original ghouls for a new generation that embraces what makes them unique and rallies people everywhere to express themselves.Monster High 2 is directed and executive produced by Todd Holland (Monster High The Movie, The Real O'Neals, Malcolm in the Middle). Since its founding in 1945, Mattel is proud to be a trusted partner in empowering children to explore the wonder of childhood and reach their full potential. The brand includes television programming and production in the United States and around the world, plus consumer products, digital, location-based experiences, publishing and feature films. Title: Is There An Opportunity With Mattel, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:MAT) 31% Undervaluation?
Text: [Key InsightsUsing the 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity, Mattel fair value estimate is US$30.85Current share price of US$21.31 suggests Mattel is potentially 31% undervaluedOur fair value estimate is 26% higher than Mattel's analyst price target of US$24.55How far off is Mattel, Inc. (NASDAQ:MAT) from its intrinsic value? Using the most recent financial data, we'll take a look at whether the stock is fairly priced by taking the expected future cash flows and discounting them to their present value. This will be done using the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model. It may sound complicated, but actually it is quite simple!Companies can be valued in a lot of ways, so we would point out that a DCF is not perfect for every situation. Anyone interested in learning a bit more about intrinsic value should have a read of the Simply Wall St analysis model. Check out our latest analysis for Mattel The MethodWe are going to use a two-stage DCF model, which, as the name states, takes into account two stages of growth. The first stage is generally a higher growth period which levels off heading towards the terminal value, captured in the second 'steady growth' period. To start off with, we need to estimate the next ten years of cash flows. Where possible we use analyst estimates, but when these aren't available we extrapolate the previous free cash flow (FCF) from the last estimate or reported value. We assume companies with shrinking free cash flow will slow their rate of shrinkage, and that companies with growing free cash flow will see their growth rate slow, over this period. We do this to reflect that growth tends to slow more in the early years than it does in later years.Generally we assume that a dollar today is more valuable than a dollar in the future, and so the sum of these future cash flows is then discounted to today's value:10-year free cash flow (FCF) forecast2024202520262027202820292030203120322033 Levered FCF ($, Millions) US$564.3mUS$734.0mUS$687.0mUS$735.0mUS$771.7mUS$803.7mUS$832.2mUS$858.2mUS$882.5mUS$905.7mGrowth Rate Estimate SourceAnalyst x4Analyst x1Analyst x1Analyst x1Est @ 5.00%Est @ 4.14%Est @ 3.54%Est @ 3.13%Est @ 2.83%Est @ 2.63% Present Value ($, Millions) Discounted @ 8.8% US$519US$620US$534US$525US$507US$485US$462US$438US$414US$391("Est" = FCF growth rate estimated by Simply Wall St)Present Value of 10-year Cash Flow (PVCF) = US$4.9bStory continuesThe second stage is also known as Terminal Value, this is the business's cash flow after the first stage. For a number of reasons a very conservative growth rate is used that cannot exceed that of a country's GDP growth. In this case we have used the 5-year average of the 10-year government bond yield (2.2%) to estimate future growth. In the same way as with the 10-year 'growth' period, we discount future cash flows to today's value, using a cost of equity of 8.8%.Terminal Value (TV)= FCF2033 × (1 + g) ÷ (r – g) = US$906m× (1 + 2.2%) ÷ (8.8%– 2.2%) = US$14bPresent Value of Terminal Value (PVTV)= TV / (1 + r)10= US$14b÷ ( 1 + 8.8%)10= US$6.0bThe total value, or equity value, is then the sum of the present value of the future cash flows, which in this case is US$11b. The last step is to then divide the equity value by the number of shares outstanding. Compared to the current share price of US$21.3, the company appears quite good value at a 31% discount to where the stock price trades currently. The assumptions in any calculation have a big impact on the valuation, so it is better to view this as a rough estimate, not precise down to the last cent.dcfThe AssumptionsWe would point out that the most important inputs to a discounted cash flow are the discount rate and of course the actual cash flows. Part of investing is coming up with your own evaluation of a company's future performance, so try the calculation yourself and check your own assumptions. The DCF also does not consider the possible cyclicality of an industry, or a company's future capital requirements, so it does not give a full picture of a company's potential performance. Given that we are looking at Mattel as potential shareholders, the cost of equity is used as the discount rate, rather than the cost of capital (or weighted average cost of capital, WACC) which accounts for debt. In this calculation we've used 8.8%, which is based on a levered beta of 1.324. Beta is a measure of a stock's volatility, compared to the market as a whole. We get our beta from the industry average beta of globally comparable companies, with an imposed limit between 0.8 and 2.0, which is a reasonable range for a stable business.SWOT Analysis for MattelStrengthDebt is well covered by earnings and cashflows.WeaknessEarnings declined over the past year.OpportunityAnnual earnings are forecast to grow faster than the American market.Trading below our estimate of fair value by more than 20%.ThreatAnnual revenue is forecast to grow slower than the American market.Moving On:Although the valuation of a company is important, it is only one of many factors that you need to assess for a company. The DCF model is not a perfect stock valuation tool. Preferably you'd apply different cases and assumptions and see how they would impact the company's valuation. For instance, if the terminal value growth rate is adjusted slightly, it can dramatically alter the overall result. What is the reason for the share price sitting below the intrinsic value? Title: MATTEL, NICKELODEON AND PARAMOUNT+ DEBUT TRAILER FOR MONSTER HIGH 2, THE SEQUEL TO THE LIVE-ACTION MUSICAL PREMIERING THURSDAY, OCT. 5
Text: [Movie will Introduce New Character Toralei, Feisty British Were-CatShare it: @Nickelodeon @Mattel @ParamountPlus @MonsterHigh #Nickelodeon #MonsterHigh2Click HERE to embed the trailer and HERE to download assets.EL SEGUNDO, Calif. and HOLLYWOOD, Calif., Sept. 15, 2023 /PRNewswire/ -- Mattel, Inc. (NASDAQ: MAT), Nickelodeon and Paramount+ today revealed the trailer and premiere date for Monster High 2, the sequel to the live-action movie musical based on the iconic Monster High franchise about the children of famous monsters and creatures. Monster High 2 will be available to stream in the U.S. on Paramount+ Thursday, October 5, and premiere on Nickelodeon that same day at 7 p.m. (ET/PT), with encores every weekend in October as part of the Monster Movie Madness stunt. The movie will also premiere later in the month on Paramount+ in select international markets where the service is available, with other international territories premiere dates to be announced later this year.MATTEL, NICKELODEON AND PARAMOUNT+ DEBUT TRAILER FOR MONSTER HIGH 2, THE SEQUEL TO THE LIVE-ACTION MUSICAL PREMIERING THURSDAY, OCT. 5Monster High 2 follows Clawdeen Wolf (Miia Harris), Draculaura (Nayah Damasen) and Frankie Stein (Ceci Balagot) as they enter sophomore year at Monster High. The power of three is put to the test as they face even bigger challenges this year—new students, new powers, evolving friendships, and an even bigger threat that could not only tear their friendship apart, but could change the world forever. The movie will also introduce new character Toralei (Salena Qureshi), a feisty British were-cat, back after a year abroad in Scaris, France.Monster High 2 also stars: Case Walker (The Other Two) as Deuce Gorgon; Marci T. House (Day of the Dead) as Headmistress Bloodgood; Scotch Ellis Loring (Firehouse Dog) as Clawdeen's dad, Apollo; Steve Valentine (Mom) as Draculaura's dad, Dracula; Jy Prishkulnik (Just Beyond) as Cleo de Nile; Lina Lecompte (Death Pursuit) as Lagoona; Justin Derickson (When the Streetlights Go On) as Heath Burns; Lilah Fitzgerald (Honey Girls) as Ghoulia; Nasiv Sall (Descendants 2) as Abbey Bominable; Bonale Fambrini (Kevin Can Wait) as Ellis; Kyra Leroux (Riverdale) as Demi Boovais; and Ana Ortiz (Love, Victor) as Zamara Prue. Additional fan-favorite characters from the Monster High universe will also be seen throughout the movie.Story continuesThe sequel follows the success of Monster High The Movie, which debuted on Oct. 6, 2022 and became the #1 kids and family movie on Paramount+ during its launch week. It reached more than 4M total viewers across its premiere weekend on linear (Nickelodeon, Nick at Nite, Nicktoons and TeenNick). In Live +3, the linear simulcast posted impressive triple-digit increases, up more than +100% with Kids 6-11 and scored double-digit increases with total viewers (+45%).The Monster High animated series will also return on Nickelodeon this fall. Mattel first introduced Monster High in 2010, and it quickly became one of the most successful and beloved kids' properties of all time. The franchise seeks to foster a more accepting world where everyone is proud to be their authentic self, which is more relevant than ever. Today, Monster High is back with a reimagined set of fangtastic characters reflected in a new set of dolls, accessories, apparel, costumes and more, inspired by the original ghouls for a new generation that embraces what makes them unique and rallies people everywhere to express themselves.Monster High 2 is directed and executive produced by Todd Holland (Monster High The Movie, The Real O'Neals, Malcolm in the Middle). Production on Monster High 2 for Nickelodeon is overseen by Zack Olin and Shauna Phelan, Co-Heads of Nickelodeon & Awesomeness Live-Action, along with executive Linda Halder.About Mattel Mattel is a leading global toy company and owner of one of the strongest catalogs of children's and family entertainment franchises in the world. We engage consumers through our portfolio of iconic brands, including Barbie®, Hot Wheels®, Fisher-Price®, American Girl®, Thomas & Friends®, UNO®, Masters of the Universe®, Monster High® and MEGA®, as well as other popular intellectual properties that we own or license in partnership with global entertainment companies. Our offerings include film and television content, gaming, music, and live events. We operate in 35 locations and our products are available in more than 150 countries in collaboration with the world's leading retail and ecommerce companies. Since its founding in 1945, Mattel is proud to be a trusted partner in empowering children to explore the wonder of childhood and reach their full potential. Visit us online at mattel.com.About NickelodeonNickelodeon, now in its 44th year, is the number-one entertainment brand for kids. It has built a diverse, global business by putting kids first in everything it does. The brand includes television programming and production in the United States and around the world, plus consumer products, digital, location-based experiences, publishing and feature films. For more information or artwork, visit http://www.nickpress.com. Nickelodeon is a part of Paramount's (Nasdaq: PARA, PARAA) global portfolio of multimedia entertainment brands.About Paramount+Paramount+, a direct-to-consumer digital subscription video on-demand and live streaming service, combines live sports, breaking news and a Mountain of Entertainment™. The premium streaming service features an expansive library of original series, hit shows and popular movies across every genre from world-renowned brands and production studios, including BET, CBS, Comedy Central, MTV, Nickelodeon, Paramount Pictures and the Smithsonian Channel. Paramount+ with SHOWTIME, the service's cornerstone plan, is also home to SHOWTIME content including scripted hits, critically acclaimed nonfiction projects, SHOWTIME SPORTS® (including industry-leading SHOWTIME Boxing) and films. This premium plan includes unmatched events and sports programming through the local live CBS stream, including golf to basketball and more, plus streaming access to CBS News Network for 24/7 news and CBS Sports HQ for sports news and analysis.For more information about Paramount+, please visit http://www.paramountplus.com and follow @ParamountPlus on social platforms.CisionView original content to download multimedia:https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mattel-nickelodeon-and-paramount-debut-trailer-for-monster-high-2-the-sequel-to-the-live-action-musical-premiering-thursday-oct-5-301929187.htmlSOURCE Nickelodeon]

Title: Is There An Opportunity With Mattel, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:MAT) 31% Undervaluation?
Text: [Key InsightsUsing the 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity, Mattel fair value estimate is US$30.85Current share price of US$21.31 suggests Mattel is potentially 31% undervaluedOur fair value estimate is 26% higher than Mattel's analyst price target of US$24.55How far off is Mattel, Inc. (NASDAQ:MAT) from its intrinsic value? Using the most recent financial data, we'll take a look at whether the stock is fairly priced by taking the expected future cash flows and discounting them to their present value. This will be done using the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model. It may sound complicated, but actually it is quite simple!Companies can be valued in a lot of ways, so we would point out that a DCF is not perfect for every situation. Anyone interested in learning a bit more about intrinsic value should have a read of the Simply Wall St analysis model. Check out our latest analysis for Mattel The MethodWe are going to use a two-stage DCF model, which, as the name states, takes into account two stages of growth. The first stage is generally a higher growth period which levels off heading towards the terminal value, captured in the second 'steady growth' period. To start off with, we need to estimate the next ten years of cash flows. Where possible we use analyst estimates, but when these aren't available we extrapolate the previous free cash flow (FCF) from the last estimate or reported value. We assume companies with shrinking free cash flow will slow their rate of shrinkage, and that companies with growing free cash flow will see their growth rate slow, over this period. We do this to reflect that growth tends to slow more in the early years than it does in later years.Generally we assume that a dollar today is more valuable than a dollar in the future, and so the sum of these future cash flows is then discounted to today's value:10-year free cash flow (FCF) forecast2024202520262027202820292030203120322033 Levered FCF ($, Millions) US$564.3mUS$734.0mUS$687.0mUS$735.0mUS$771.7mUS$803.7mUS$832.2mUS$858.2mUS$882.5mUS$905.7mGrowth Rate Estimate SourceAnalyst x4Analyst x1Analyst x1Analyst x1Est @ 5.00%Est @ 4.14%Est @ 3.54%Est @ 3.13%Est @ 2.83%Est @ 2.63% Present Value ($, Millions) Discounted @ 8.8% US$519US$620US$534US$525US$507US$485US$462US$438US$414US$391("Est" = FCF growth rate estimated by Simply Wall St)Present Value of 10-year Cash Flow (PVCF) = US$4.9bStory continuesThe second stage is also known as Terminal Value, this is the business's cash flow after the first stage. For a number of reasons a very conservative growth rate is used that cannot exceed that of a country's GDP growth. In this case we have used the 5-year average of the 10-year government bond yield (2.2%) to estimate future growth. In the same way as with the 10-year 'growth' period, we discount future cash flows to today's value, using a cost of equity of 8.8%.Terminal Value (TV)= FCF2033 × (1 + g) ÷ (r – g) = US$906m× (1 + 2.2%) ÷ (8.8%– 2.2%) = US$14bPresent Value of Terminal Value (PVTV)= TV / (1 + r)10= US$14b÷ ( 1 + 8.8%)10= US$6.0bThe total value, or equity value, is then the sum of the present value of the future cash flows, which in this case is US$11b. The last step is to then divide the equity value by the number of shares outstanding. Compared to the current share price of US$21.3, the company appears quite good value at a 31% discount to where the stock price trades currently. The assumptions in any calculation have a big impact on the valuation, so it is better to view this as a rough estimate, not precise down to the last cent.dcfThe AssumptionsWe would point out that the most important inputs to a discounted cash flow are the discount rate and of course the actual cash flows. Part of investing is coming up with your own evaluation of a company's future performance, so try the calculation yourself and check your own assumptions. The DCF also does not consider the possible cyclicality of an industry, or a company's future capital requirements, so it does not give a full picture of a company's potential performance. Given that we are looking at Mattel as potential shareholders, the cost of equity is used as the discount rate, rather than the cost of capital (or weighted average cost of capital, WACC) which accounts for debt. In this calculation we've used 8.8%, which is based on a levered beta of 1.324. Beta is a measure of a stock's volatility, compared to the market as a whole. We get our beta from the industry average beta of globally comparable companies, with an imposed limit between 0.8 and 2.0, which is a reasonable range for a stable business.SWOT Analysis for MattelStrengthDebt is well covered by earnings and cashflows.WeaknessEarnings declined over the past year.OpportunityAnnual earnings are forecast to grow faster than the American market.Trading below our estimate of fair value by more than 20%.ThreatAnnual revenue is forecast to grow slower than the American market.Moving On:Although the valuation of a company is important, it is only one of many factors that you need to assess for a company. The DCF model is not a perfect stock valuation tool. Preferably you'd apply different cases and assumptions and see how they would impact the company's valuation. For instance, if the terminal value growth rate is adjusted slightly, it can dramatically alter the overall result. What is the reason for the share price sitting below the intrinsic value? Title: MATTEL, NICKELODEON AND PARAMOUNT+ DEBUT TRAILER FOR MONSTER HIGH 2, THE SEQUEL TO THE LIVE-ACTION MUSICAL PREMIERING THURSDAY, OCT. 5
Text: [Movie will Introduce New Character Toralei, Feisty British Were-CatShare it: @Nickelodeon @Mattel @ParamountPlus @MonsterHigh #Nickelodeon #MonsterHigh2Click HERE to embed the trailer and HERE to download assets.EL SEGUNDO, Calif. and HOLLYWOOD, Calif., Sept. 15, 2023 /PRNewswire/ -- Mattel, Inc. (NASDAQ: MAT), Nickelodeon and Paramount+ today revealed the trailer and premiere date for Monster High 2, the sequel to the live-action movie musical based on the iconic Monster High franchise about the children of famous monsters and creatures. Monster High 2 will be available to stream in the U.S. on Paramount+ Thursday, October 5, and premiere on Nickelodeon that same day at 7 p.m. (ET/PT), with encores every weekend in October as part of the Monster Movie Madness stunt. The movie will also premiere later in the month on Paramount+ in select international markets where the service is available, with other international territories premiere dates to be announced later this year.MATTEL, NICKELODEON AND PARAMOUNT+ DEBUT TRAILER FOR MONSTER HIGH 2, THE SEQUEL TO THE LIVE-ACTION MUSICAL PREMIERING THURSDAY, OCT. 5Monster High 2 follows Clawdeen Wolf (Miia Harris), Draculaura (Nayah Damasen) and Frankie Stein (Ceci Balagot) as they enter sophomore year at Monster High. The power of three is put to the test as they face even bigger challenges this year—new students, new powers, evolving friendships, and an even bigger threat that could not only tear their friendship apart, but could change the world forever. The movie will also introduce new character Toralei (Salena Qureshi), a feisty British were-cat, back after a year abroad in Scaris, France.Monster High 2 also stars: Case Walker (The Other Two) as Deuce Gorgon; Marci T. House (Day of the Dead) as Headmistress Bloodgood; Scotch Ellis Loring (Firehouse Dog) as Clawdeen's dad, Apollo; Steve Valentine (Mom) as Draculaura's dad, Dracula; Jy Prishkulnik (Just Beyond) as Cleo de Nile; Lina Lecompte (Death Pursuit) as Lagoona; Justin Derickson (When the Streetlights Go On) as Heath Burns; Lilah Fitzgerald (Honey Girls) as Ghoulia; Nasiv Sall (Descendants 2) as Abbey Bominable; Bonale Fambrini (Kevin Can Wait) as Ellis; Kyra Leroux (Riverdale) as Demi Boovais; and Ana Ortiz (Love, Victor) as Zamara Prue. Additional fan-favorite characters from the Monster High universe will also be seen throughout the movie.Story continuesThe sequel follows the success of Monster High The Movie, which debuted on Oct. 6, 2022 and became the #1 kids and family movie on Paramount+ during its launch week. It reached more than 4M total viewers across its premiere weekend on linear (Nickelodeon, Nick at Nite, Nicktoons and TeenNick). In Live +3, the linear simulcast posted impressive triple-digit increases, up more than +100% with Kids 6-11 and scored double-digit increases with total viewers (+45%).The Monster High animated series will also return on Nickelodeon this fall. Mattel first introduced Monster High in 2010, and it quickly became one of the most successful and beloved kids' properties of all time. The franchise seeks to foster a more accepting world where everyone is proud to be their authentic self, which is more relevant than ever. Today, Monster High is back with a reimagined set of fangtastic characters reflected in a new set of dolls, accessories, apparel, costumes and more, inspired by the original ghouls for a new generation that embraces what makes them unique and rallies people everywhere to express themselves.Monster High 2 is directed and executive produced by Todd Holland (Monster High The Movie, The Real O'Neals, Malcolm in the Middle). Production on Monster High 2 for Nickelodeon is overseen by Zack Olin and Shauna Phelan, Co-Heads of Nickelodeon & Awesomeness Live-Action, along with executive Linda Halder.About Mattel Mattel is a leading global toy company and owner of one of the strongest catalogs of children's and family entertainment franchises in the world. We engage consumers through our portfolio of iconic brands, including Barbie®, Hot Wheels®, Fisher-Price®, American Girl®, Thomas & Friends®, UNO®, Masters of the Universe®, Monster High® and MEGA®, as well as other popular intellectual properties that we own or license in partnership with global entertainment companies. Our offerings include film and television content, gaming, music, and live events. We operate in 35 locations and our products are available in more than 150 countries in collaboration with the world's leading retail and ecommerce companies. Since its founding in 1945, Mattel is proud to be a trusted partner in empowering children to explore the wonder of childhood and reach their full potential. Visit us online at mattel.com.About NickelodeonNickelodeon, now in its 44th year, is the number-one entertainment brand for kids. It has built a diverse, global business by putting kids first in everything it does. The brand includes television programming and production in the United States and around the world, plus consumer products, digital, location-based experiences, publishing and feature films. For more information or artwork, visit http://www.nickpress.com. Nickelodeon is a part of Paramount's (Nasdaq: PARA, PARAA) global portfolio of multimedia entertainment brands.About Paramount+Paramount+, a direct-to-consumer digital subscription video on-demand and live streaming service, combines live sports, breaking news and a Mountain of Entertainment™. The premium streaming service features an expansive library of original series, hit shows and popular movies across every genre from world-renowned brands and production studios, including BET, CBS, Comedy Central, MTV, Nickelodeon, Paramount Pictures and the Smithsonian Channel. Paramount+ with SHOWTIME, the service's cornerstone plan, is also home to SHOWTIME content including scripted hits, critically acclaimed nonfiction projects, SHOWTIME SPORTS® (including industry-leading SHOWTIME Boxing) and films. This premium plan includes unmatched events and sports programming through the local live CBS stream, including golf to basketball and more, plus streaming access to CBS News Network for 24/7 news and CBS Sports HQ for sports news and analysis.For more information about Paramount+, please visit http://www.paramountplus.com and follow @ParamountPlus on social platforms.CisionView original content to download multimedia:https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mattel-nickelodeon-and-paramount-debut-trailer-for-monster-high-2-the-sequel-to-the-live-action-musical-premiering-thursday-oct-5-301929187.htmlSOURCE Nickelodeon]

Title: Is There An Opportunity With Mattel, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:MAT) 31% Undervaluation?
Text: [Key InsightsUsing the 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity, Mattel fair value estimate is US$30.85Current share price of US$21.31 suggests Mattel is potentially 31% undervaluedOur fair value estimate is 26% higher than Mattel's analyst price target of US$24.55How far off is Mattel, Inc. (NASDAQ:MAT) from its intrinsic value? Using the most recent financial data, we'll take a look at whether the stock is fairly priced by taking the expected future cash flows and discounting them to their present value. This will be done using the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model. It may sound complicated, but actually it is quite simple!Companies can be valued in a lot of ways, so we would point out that a DCF is not perfect for every situation. Anyone interested in learning a bit more about intrinsic value should have a read of the Simply Wall St analysis model. Check out our latest analysis for Mattel The MethodWe are going to use a two-stage DCF model, which, as the name states, takes into account two stages of growth. The first stage is generally a higher growth period which levels off heading towards the terminal value, captured in the second 'steady growth' period. To start off with, we need to estimate the next ten years of cash flows. Where possible we use analyst estimates, but when these aren't available we extrapolate the previous free cash flow (FCF) from the last estimate or reported value. We assume companies with shrinking free cash flow will slow their rate of shrinkage, and that companies with growing free cash flow will see their growth rate slow, over this period. We do this to reflect that growth tends to slow more in the early years than it does in later years.Generally we assume that a dollar today is more valuable than a dollar in the future, and so the sum of these future cash flows is then discounted to today's value:10-year free cash flow (FCF) forecast2024202520262027202820292030203120322033 Levered FCF ($, Millions) US$564.3mUS$734.0mUS$687.0mUS$735.0mUS$771.7mUS$803.7mUS$832.2mUS$858.2mUS$882.5mUS$905.7mGrowth Rate Estimate SourceAnalyst x4Analyst x1Analyst x1Analyst x1Est @ 5.00%Est @ 4.14%Est @ 3.54%Est @ 3.13%Est @ 2.83%Est @ 2.63% Present Value ($, Millions) Discounted @ 8.8% US$519US$620US$534US$525US$507US$485US$462US$438US$414US$391("Est" = FCF growth rate estimated by Simply Wall St)Present Value of 10-year Cash Flow (PVCF) = US$4.9bStory continuesThe second stage is also known as Terminal Value, this is the business's cash flow after the first stage. For a number of reasons a very conservative growth rate is used that cannot exceed that of a country's GDP growth. In this case we have used the 5-year average of the 10-year government bond yield (2.2%) to estimate future growth. In the same way as with the 10-year 'growth' period, we discount future cash flows to today's value, using a cost of equity of 8.8%.Terminal Value (TV)= FCF2033 × (1 + g) ÷ (r – g) = US$906m× (1 + 2.2%) ÷ (8.8%– 2.2%) = US$14bPresent Value of Terminal Value (PVTV)= TV / (1 + r)10= US$14b÷ ( 1 + 8.8%)10= US$6.0bThe total value, or equity value, is then the sum of the present value of the future cash flows, which in this case is US$11b. The last step is to then divide the equity value by the number of shares outstanding. Compared to the current share price of US$21.3, the company appears quite good value at a 31% discount to where the stock price trades currently. The assumptions in any calculation have a big impact on the valuation, so it is better to view this as a rough estimate, not precise down to the last cent.dcfThe AssumptionsWe would point out that the most important inputs to a discounted cash flow are the discount rate and of course the actual cash flows. Part of investing is coming up with your own evaluation of a company's future performance, so try the calculation yourself and check your own assumptions. The DCF also does not consider the possible cyclicality of an industry, or a company's future capital requirements, so it does not give a full picture of a company's potential performance. Given that we are looking at Mattel as potential shareholders, the cost of equity is used as the discount rate, rather than the cost of capital (or weighted average cost of capital, WACC) which accounts for debt. In this calculation we've used 8.8%, which is based on a levered beta of 1.324. Beta is a measure of a stock's volatility, compared to the market as a whole. We get our beta from the industry average beta of globally comparable companies, with an imposed limit between 0.8 and 2.0, which is a reasonable range for a stable business.SWOT Analysis for MattelStrengthDebt is well covered by earnings and cashflows.WeaknessEarnings declined over the past year.OpportunityAnnual earnings are forecast to grow faster than the American market.Trading below our estimate of fair value by more than 20%.ThreatAnnual revenue is forecast to grow slower than the American market.Moving On:Although the valuation of a company is important, it is only one of many factors that you need to assess for a company. The DCF model is not a perfect stock valuation tool. Preferably you'd apply different cases and assumptions and see how they would impact the company's valuation. For instance, if the terminal value growth rate is adjusted slightly, it can dramatically alter the overall result. What is the reason for the share price sitting below the intrinsic value? Title: MATTEL, NICKELODEON AND PARAMOUNT+ DEBUT TRAILER FOR MONSTER HIGH 2, THE SEQUEL TO THE LIVE-ACTION MUSICAL PREMIERING THURSDAY, OCT. 5
Text: [Movie will Introduce New Character Toralei, Feisty British Were-CatShare it: @Nickelodeon @Mattel @ParamountPlus @MonsterHigh #Nickelodeon #MonsterHigh2Click HERE to embed the trailer and HERE to download assets.EL SEGUNDO, Calif. and HOLLYWOOD, Calif., Sept. 15, 2023 /PRNewswire/ -- Mattel, Inc. (NASDAQ: MAT), Nickelodeon and Paramount+ today revealed the trailer and premiere date for Monster High 2, the sequel to the live-action movie musical based on the iconic Monster High franchise about the children of famous monsters and creatures. Monster High 2 will be available to stream in the U.S. on Paramount+ Thursday, October 5, and premiere on Nickelodeon that same day at 7 p.m. (ET/PT), with encores every weekend in October as part of the Monster Movie Madness stunt. The movie will also premiere later in the month on Paramount+ in select international markets where the service is available, with other international territories premiere dates to be announced later this year.MATTEL, NICKELODEON AND PARAMOUNT+ DEBUT TRAILER FOR MONSTER HIGH 2, THE SEQUEL TO THE LIVE-ACTION MUSICAL PREMIERING THURSDAY, OCT. 5Monster High 2 follows Clawdeen Wolf (Miia Harris), Draculaura (Nayah Damasen) and Frankie Stein (Ceci Balagot) as they enter sophomore year at Monster High. The power of three is put to the test as they face even bigger challenges this year—new students, new powers, evolving friendships, and an even bigger threat that could not only tear their friendship apart, but could change the world forever. The movie will also introduce new character Toralei (Salena Qureshi), a feisty British were-cat, back after a year abroad in Scaris, France.Monster High 2 also stars: Case Walker (The Other Two) as Deuce Gorgon; Marci T. House (Day of the Dead) as Headmistress Bloodgood; Scotch Ellis Loring (Firehouse Dog) as Clawdeen's dad, Apollo; Steve Valentine (Mom) as Draculaura's dad, Dracula; Jy Prishkulnik (Just Beyond) as Cleo de Nile; Lina Lecompte (Death Pursuit) as Lagoona; Justin Derickson (When the Streetlights Go On) as Heath Burns; Lilah Fitzgerald (Honey Girls) as Ghoulia; Nasiv Sall (Descendants 2) as Abbey Bominable; Bonale Fambrini (Kevin Can Wait) as Ellis; Kyra Leroux (Riverdale) as Demi Boovais; and Ana Ortiz (Love, Victor) as Zamara Prue. Additional fan-favorite characters from the Monster High universe will also be seen throughout the movie.Story continuesThe sequel follows the success of Monster High The Movie, which debuted on Oct. 6, 2022 and became the #1 kids and family movie on Paramount+ during its launch week. It reached more than 4M total viewers across its premiere weekend on linear (Nickelodeon, Nick at Nite, Nicktoons and TeenNick). In Live +3, the linear simulcast posted impressive triple-digit increases, up more than +100% with Kids 6-11 and scored double-digit increases with total viewers (+45%).The Monster High animated series will also return on Nickelodeon this fall. Mattel first introduced Monster High in 2010, and it quickly became one of the most successful and beloved kids' properties of all time. The franchise seeks to foster a more accepting world where everyone is proud to be their authentic self, which is more relevant than ever. Today, Monster High is back with a reimagined set of fangtastic characters reflected in a new set of dolls, accessories, apparel, costumes and more, inspired by the original ghouls for a new generation that embraces what makes them unique and rallies people everywhere to express themselves.Monster High 2 is directed and executive produced by Todd Holland (Monster High The Movie, The Real O'Neals, Malcolm in the Middle). Phil Breman, Vice President of Live Action Development at Mattel Television, Adam Bonnett (Descendants, Zombies, Masters of the Universe) and Fred Soulie serve as executive producers. Shawn Williamson (The Good Doctor) and Arielle Boisvert (Upload) from Brightlight Pictures also serve as executive producers with David Magee serving as producer. The sequel teleplay is written by Matt & Billy Eddy (Teen Beach, Invisible Sister, Zapped), with story by Todd Holland & Matt & Billy Eddy. Production on Monster High 2 for Nickelodeon is overseen by Zack Olin and Shauna Phelan, Co-Heads of Nickelodeon & Awesomeness Live-Action, along with executive Linda Halder.About Mattel Mattel is a leading global toy company and owner of one of the strongest catalogs of children's and family entertainment franchises in the world. We create innovative products and experiences that inspire, entertain, and develop children through play. We engage consumers through our portfolio of iconic brands, including Barbie®, Hot Wheels®, Fisher-Price®, American Girl®, Thomas & Friends®, UNO®, Masters of the Universe®, Monster High® and MEGA®, as well as other popular intellectual properties that we own or license in partnership with global entertainment companies. Our offerings include film and television content, gaming, music, and live events. We operate in 35 locations and our products are available in more than 150 countries in collaboration with the world's leading retail and ecommerce companies. Since its founding in 1945, Mattel is proud to be a trusted partner in empowering children to explore the wonder of childhood and reach their full potential. Visit us online at mattel.com.About NickelodeonNickelodeon, now in its 44th year, is the number-one entertainment brand for kids. It has built a diverse, global business by putting kids first in everything it does. The brand includes television programming and production in the United States and around the world, plus consumer products, digital, location-based experiences, publishing and feature films. For more information or artwork, visit http://www.nickpress.com. Nickelodeon is a part of Paramount's (Nasdaq: PARA, PARAA) global portfolio of multimedia entertainment brands.About Paramount+Paramount+, a direct-to-consumer digital subscription video on-demand and live streaming service, combines live sports, breaking news and a Mountain of Entertainment™. The premium streaming service features an expansive library of original series, hit shows and popular movies across every genre from world-renowned brands and production studios, including BET, CBS, Comedy Central, MTV, Nickelodeon, Paramount Pictures and the Smithsonian Channel. Paramount+ with SHOWTIME, the service's cornerstone plan, is also home to SHOWTIME content including scripted hits, critically acclaimed nonfiction projects, SHOWTIME SPORTS® (including industry-leading SHOWTIME Boxing) and films. This premium plan includes unmatched events and sports programming through the local live CBS stream, including golf to basketball and more, plus streaming access to CBS News Network for 24/7 news and CBS Sports HQ for sports news and analysis.For more information about Paramount+, please visit http://www.paramountplus.com and follow @ParamountPlus on social platforms.CisionView original content to download multimedia:https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/mattel-nickelodeon-and-paramount-debut-trailer-for-monster-high-2-the-sequel-to-the-live-action-musical-premiering-thursday-oct-5-301929187.htmlSOURCE Nickelodeon]
